market_regime: Oil-driven inflation shock (WTI +27% 1m) amid Middle East conflict is pushing 10Y yields up and reviving Fed rate-hike odds, pressuring long-duration mega-cap tech (QQQ -3.7% 1m) even as the 3m AI-led uptrend stays intact. Leadership has rotated toward energy, financials, and health care while consumer discretionary and communication lag. VIX is subdued (~18.6), so this looks like a rotation/reflation regime rather than a broad risk-off event.

themes.name: Energy & Oil Shock
themes.thesis: WTI is up 27% in one month and 20% over three, with Middle East conflict/oil-supply headlines and a World Bank growth-cut warning. Energy is the top sector (+11.3% 1m) and rising rate-hike odds are being explicitly tied to the oil spike, favoring integrated majors, E&Ps, and oilfield services with direct crude leverage.

themes.name: AI Data Center Power & Infrastructure
themes.thesis: OpenAI cloud spend reported at $750B and Alphabet raising AI capex to $205B confirm a durable buildout, with headlines steering money toward the 'picks and shovels' layer (power, cooling, electrical, fiber) rather than chips alone. Congress is advancing data-center energy bills, underscoring grid/power constraints that benefit electrical equipment and independent power producers.

themes.name: Semiconductors & US Reshoring
themes.thesis: Digest cites a semiconductor-led futures recovery, record short interest raising squeeze potential, and heavy state/federal reshoring investment (Texas, Oregon). AI infrastructure spend hit $89.7B with ARM passing x86, supporting compute, memory, and fab-equipment demand despite the near-term tech pullback.

themes.name: Financials on Higher-for-Longer Rates
themes.thesis: Rising 10Y yields (+15.4% 3m) and surging Fed rate-hike odds widen net interest margins, while financials are a persistent leader (+4.8% 1m, +10.9% 3m). Banks and capital-markets names benefit from a steeper curve and 'investors want a bigger reward for lending' dynamic in the digest.

avoid.reason: Weakest sector (-4.9% 1m, -4.0% 3m); rising rates, oil-driven inflation squeezing consumers, and hike odds are direct headwinds.

avoid.what: Long-duration/high-multiple mega-cap tech and communication services
avoid.reason: QQQ -3.7% 1m and Communication -9.4% 3m; rising yields compress valuations and Reuters/CNBC flag AI capex pressuring Big Tech free cash flow and bond-market anxiety.
Lagging (-0.4% 1m, -2.9% 3m) with margin pressure from higher input/energy costs and no rate tailwind in this reflation rotation.
Gold is down 20% over 3m against rising real yields and a firmer dollar; the higher-for-longer backdrop is a structural headwind.
Strong secular headlines but few liquid US-listed pure plays and no confirming price momentum; thesis is early and speculative.
